source.title: ASCENT: First-Order Optimal Fine-Tuning with Recalibration for Safety--Utility Co-Enhancement
source.authors: Wei-Wei Qi; Chong-Yu Wang; Tian-Hang Zheng; Ze-Feng Wu; Zhi-Ling Guo; Xiao-Jun Jia; Zhong-Jie Ba; Kui Ren

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether ordinary downstream fine-tuning affects safety behavior, using task fine-tuning and harmful-prompt attack success rate on evaluated chat models.
record.gate_note: Rows record vanilla Task FT results in Table 2. The matched-control table repeats those Task FT results. Results for ASCENT and other safety-preserving methods are not rows for V2 because they include additional interventions. The study does not measure response-position KL, prefilling, suffixes, decoding changes, or harmful-example fine-tuning.
record.test_reason: Besides proposing a mitigation method (ASCENT), the paper reports vanilla benign task fine-tuning (rank-32 LoRA on SAMSum, AG News, GSM8K, OpenBookQA). It gives JailbreakBench ASR for this condition (Table 2/Table 8) alongside the un-fine-tuned Original ASR (Table 1). That directly bears on whether benign fine-tuning raises harmful compliance, the same question and broadly the same design as Qi et al. 2024.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors take prior evidence (Qi et al. 2024) that benign fine-tuning degrades safety as motivation. They conclude ASCENT achieves safety–utility co-enhancement, lowering ASR below Original in all settings while existing safety-preserving baselines never reduce ASR below Original.
record.recipe_differences: Uses vanilla rank-32 LoRA downstream task fine-tuning and jailbreak ASR evaluation; the paper does not provide enough detail about the original source's exact recipe to establish an exact match. Here the task fine-tuning uses 2,000 sampled examples and 80 optimizer steps.
record.problems: The vanilla Task FT results used here cover two models and four downstream tasks, rather than all four models in the main evaluation. No uncertainty estimates are reported for these values.
record.rows_left_out: Table 8 repeats the Task FT values already recorded from Table 2. Safety-preserving method and ASCENT outcomes in Tables 1–3 and 6–8 were not recorded as vanilla benign fine-tuning results.

untested.parts: No carefully selected (adversarially chosen) benign data. Vanilla Task FT is reported numerically only for Llama-3.1-8B and Qwen3-30B-A3B, and only on JailbreakBench, not WildJailbreak or the StrongREJECT attacks.
No per-token KL or position analysis.
No prefilling, suffix or decoding attacks. TAP/PAP/RAINBOW/AutoDAN-Turbo results are for safety-preserving methods, not a test of opening-token bypass.
The method uses a rank-r safety-gradient subspace but does not test whether a small set of existing weights carries safety.
Not tested; ASCENT is not a token-depth deepening method.

missing.what: Vanilla task fine-tuning (FT) ASR for Qwen2.5-7B-it and Gemma-3-12B-it on all four tasks, shown only graphically; Original ASR is 39.5 and 37.0 respectively.

record.verdict_notes: I keep T1 because the design (benign task fine-tuning, judged ASR) matches the original, though the datasets differ and LoRA is used. Observed vs partial was set by magnitude: ≥7.5-point rises are observed, 4–5.5-point rises are partial. No variance is reported; a single seed with n=200 is implied. ASR is measured on JailbreakBench jailbreak prompts, where the Original models already show 24–39% ASR, rather than on plain harmful instructions. All four safety-preserving baselines (SafeLoRA, SaLoRA, GuardSpace, SPA) also end with ASR at or above Original in every setting (Table 1). That is consistent with V2 but involves added interventions, so it is not recorded as rows.

versions.untested_parts: Harmful-example fine-tuning and compliance after fine-tuning on harmful examples.
No separate test of carefully selected benign data; vanilla Task FT is reported for two models and four downstream tasks.
Per-token KL divergence across response positions.
Compliant-token prefilling, adversarial suffixes, and decoding changes as safety bypasses.
Whether a small set of existing weights or ranks carries safety behavior; rank-constrained safety calibration is not a test of that localization claim.
Whether data or training objectives cause safety to be shallow in the response.
Whether safety training spread beyond the first response tokens deepens safety or remains robust to bypasses.
